utility.notes: Marina is a well-documented Monterey County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

value.name: Central Coast Community Energy (3CE)
value.notes: 3CE's own official site confirms it serves Monterey County, including Marina, as part of its 5-county, 33-community service area. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

permit_url.notes: The fetched page covers only general building permit requirements; solar-specific detail (the 'Solar Eligibility Checklist for Expedited Plan Check / Permit Application' form referenced via search) was not itself confirmed on this page.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Marina/Monterey County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Solar PV Standard Plan and supporting documentation
Diagram of the roof layout of all panels/modules, clear access pathways, and approximate locations of electrical disconnecting means and roof access points

required_documents.notes: From the City's own 'Eligibility Checklist for Expedited Solar Photovoltaic Permitting for One- and Two-Family Dwellings', which requires system size 10kW AC CEC or less, roof-mounted, and utility-interactive without battery storage; larger or ineligible projects go through standard plan review instead.

value: Schedule an inspection through Online Permitting (if the permit was submitted online), by email, or by calling the Inspection Line at 831-884-1241

inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Services inspection scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited Permit Process for Small Residential Rooftop Solar Systems (municipal code Chapter 15.38)
